sections.content: I, RAJESH MEHRA, son of [FATHER'S NAME OF RAJESH MEHRA], aged 68 years, resident of [FULL RESIDENTIAL ADDRESS OF RAJESH MEHRA, KOLKATA, WEST BENGAL], do hereby declare this to be my last Will and Testament, and I revoke all wills and testamentary writings previously made by me, as more particularly set out below.

I declare that I am of sound mind, sound memory and sound understanding, and that I am making this Will out of my own free will and volition, voluntarily, without any coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation or persuasion of any kind from any person whatsoever. I am fully aware of the nature and extent of my assets and of the persons who are the natural objects of my bounty, and I am executing this Will with full appreciation of its contents and consequences.

I hereby revoke all wills, codicils and other testamentary dispositions of whatsoever nature made by me at any time prior to the date of this Will. This revocation is confined strictly to testamentary instruments executed by me before the date of this Will, and nothing in this clause shall be construed as a purported revocation of, or restriction upon, any testamentary instrument that I may execute after the date hereof.

I am a Hindu by religion. I am married to my wife, Sunita Mehra (hereinafter also referred to as "Sunita"). I have two children, namely, my son, Arjun Mehra (hereinafter also referred to as "Arjun"), and my daughter, Riya Mehra (hereinafter also referred to as "Riya"). I have no other spouse, child or dependant, whether by birth, adoption or otherwise, save and except as stated above. If this is not accurate as to any dependant of mine, [CLIENT] must confirm the same and this Will shall be revised accordingly.

The assets comprised in my estate as on the date of this Will, to the best of my knowledge and belief, include the following, without prejudice to any other asset that I may own or acquire and which shall in any event fall within the residue of my estate:

(a) Residential flat situated at [FULL DESCRIPTION AND ADDRESS OF THE KOLKATA FLAT, INCLUDING FLAT NO., FLOOR, BUILDING/SOCIETY NAME, MOUZA, WARD, KOLKATA MUNICIPAL CORPORATION DETAILS AND REGISTRATION PARTICULARS OF TITLE], presently occupied by me and my wife, Sunita Mehra, and asserted by me to be of a market value of approximately Rs. 1,50,00,000/- (Rupees One Crore Fifty Lakh only).

(b) Plot of land situated at [FULL DESCRIPTION AND ADDRESS OF THE SILIGURI PLOT, INCLUDING PLOT/DAG NO., KHATIAN NO., MOUZA, AND REGISTRATION PARTICULARS OF TITLE], asserted by me to be of a market value of approximately Rs. 80,00,000/- (Rupees Eighty Lakh only).

(c) Bank fixed deposits and savings bank accounts held with [NAME OF BANK(S) AND BRANCH(ES)], account numbers [ACCOUNT NUMBER(S)] and fixed deposit receipt numbers [FDR NUMBER(S)], asserted by me to be of an aggregate approximate value of Rs. 40,00,000/- (Rupees Forty Lakh only) as on the date of this Will.

(d) Mutual fund investments held with [NAME OF ASSET MANAGEMENT COMPANY(IES)/FOLIO NUMBER(S)], asserted by me to be of an aggregate approximate value of Rs. 25,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty-Five Lakh only) as on the date of this Will.

(e) Gold jewellery in my personal possession and ownership, more particularly described in [SCHEDULE/INVENTORY OF JEWELLERY, IF ANY, TO BE ANNEXED], asserted by me to be of an aggregate approximate value of Rs. 15,00,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Lakh only).

(f) 30% (thirty percent) shareholding, comprising [NUMBER OF SHARES] equity shares of [FACE VALUE PER SHARE] each, held by me in Mehra Trading Private Limited, a company incorporated under the Companies Act and having its registered office at [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS OF MEHRA TRADING PRIVATE LIMITED], bearing CIN [CIN NUMBER].

The values stated above are asserted by me, Rajesh Mehra, as of the date of this Will and are recorded for identification and convenience only; they do not bind my estate to any valuation for the purposes of probate, succession or taxation.

1. I give and bequeath the residential flat described in paragraph (a) of the Schedule of Assets to my wife, Sunita Mehra, for her lifetime only, as a life interest, with the remainder thereafter to my son, Arjun Mehra, and my daughter, Riya Mehra, in equal shares of 1/2 (one-half) each, absolutely, as more particularly set out in the section titled LIFE INTEREST AND REMAINDER below.

2. I give, devise and bequeath the plot of land described in paragraph (b) of the Schedule of Assets to my son, Arjun Mehra, absolutely and forever.

3. I give and bequeath the bank fixed deposits and savings described in paragraph (c) of the Schedule of Assets to my son, Arjun Mehra, and my daughter, Riya Mehra, in equal shares of 1/2 (one-half) each, absolutely.

4. I give and bequeath the mutual fund investments described in paragraph (d) of the Schedule of Assets to my son, Arjun Mehra, and my daughter, Riya Mehra, in equal shares of 1/2 (one-half) each, absolutely.

5. I give and bequeath all my gold jewellery described in paragraph (e) of the Schedule of Assets to my daughter, Riya Mehra, absolutely.

6. I give, devise and bequeath my entire 30% (thirty percent) shareholding in Mehra Trading Private Limited, described in paragraph (f) of the Schedule of Assets, to my son, Arjun Mehra, and my daughter, Riya Mehra, in equal shares of 1/2 (one-half) each, absolutely, PROVIDED THAT the transmission of such shares to Arjun and Riya shall be subject to the Articles of Association of Mehra Trading Private Limited, including any right of pre-emption, restriction on transfer, or requirement of Board approval contained therein, and to applicable law, and my Executor shall take all steps reasonably necessary to give effect to such transmission consistently with the said Articles.

In respect of the residential flat described in paragraph (a) of the Schedule of Assets, I direct as follows:

(a) My wife, Sunita Mehra, shall hold a life interest in the said flat and shall be entitled, for the duration of her natural life, to the exclusive possession, use and occupation of the said flat, and to receive all rents, profits and income, if any, arising from the said flat should she choose to let it out in whole or in part.

(b) Sunita Mehra, as life tenant, shall be responsible for and shall pay, out of her own funds or out of the income of the said flat, all outgoings in respect of the said flat, including property tax, maintenance charges, society charges, insurance premiums, and costs of ordinary repair and upkeep, for so long as her life interest subsists.

(c) Sunita Mehra shall NOT have the power to sell, transfer, mortgage, charge, lease for a term exceeding [PERIOD, e.g., eleven months] , or otherwise encumber or alienate the said flat or her life interest therein, it being my express intention that her interest is limited strictly to a life interest without any power of alienation.

(d) Upon the death of Sunita Mehra, the said flat shall pass to and vest absolutely in my son, Arjun Mehra, and my daughter, Riya Mehra, in equal shares of 1/2 (one-half) each, as remaindermen, free from the life interest.

(e) If my wife, Sunita Mehra, predeceases me, the life interest provided for in this section shall not arise, and the said flat shall, upon my death, pass directly and absolutely to my son, Arjun Mehra, and my daughter, Riya Mehra, in equal shares of 1/2 (one-half) each, subject to the substitutionary provisions set out in the section titled SUBSTITUTIONARY AND SURVIVORSHIP PROVISIONS below.

1. If my son, Arjun Mehra, predeceases me, or predeceases my wife, Sunita Mehra, in the case of the remainder interest in the flat, then the share or interest that Arjun would otherwise have taken under this Will shall pass to and vest absolutely, in equal shares per stirpes, in the children of Arjun Mehra living at the relevant time. If Arjun Mehra predeceases me or, as the case may be, predeceases Sunita Mehra, without leaving any surviving child, then his share shall pass to and vest absolutely in my daughter, Riya Mehra, or, if she has predeceased in like manner without leaving any surviving child, in accordance with paragraph 3 below.

2. If my daughter, Riya Mehra, predeceases me, or predeceases my wife, Sunita Mehra, in the case of the remainder interest in the flat, then the share or interest that Riya would otherwise have taken under this Will shall pass to and vest absolutely, in equal shares per stirpes, in the children of Riya Mehra living at the relevant time. If Riya Mehra predeceases me or, as the case may be, predeceases Sunita Mehra, without leaving any surviving child, then her share shall pass to and vest absolutely in my son, Arjun Mehra, or, if he has predeceased in like manner without leaving any surviving child, in accordance with paragraph 3 below.

3. If both Arjun Mehra and Riya Mehra predecease me (or, as regards the remainder interest in the flat, predecease Sunita Mehra) and neither leaves any surviving child, then the entire estate, or the relevant share or interest, as the case may be, shall devolve upon my heirs determined in accordance with the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as if I had died intestate in respect of that share or interest.

4. If my wife, Sunita Mehra, predeceases me, the life interest bequeathed to her under this Will shall lapse and shall not form part of her estate, and the property in respect of which such life interest was created shall devolve as provided in the section titled LIFE INTEREST AND REMAINDER above.

I direct my Executor to pay, out of my residuary estate, all my just debts, funeral and last rites expenses, and all taxes, duties and testamentary expenses (including probate expenses, if applicable) that may be outstanding or that may arise as a consequence of my death, before making any distribution of my estate to the beneficiaries named in this Will. Should the residuary estate be insufficient for this purpose, my Executor shall be entitled to realise such other assets of my estate, in such order as my Executor considers appropriate, as may be necessary to discharge such debts, expenses and taxes.

I give, devise and bequeath all the rest, residue and remainder of my estate, of whatsoever nature and wheresoever situate, including any property acquired by me after the date of execution of this Will and any property not effectively or specifically disposed of under this Will, to my son, Arjun Mehra, and my daughter, Riya Mehra, in equal shares of 1/2 (one-half) each, absolutely, subject to the substitutionary provisions set out above in the event of either of them predeceasing me.

If any clause, provision or part of this Will is held by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, void or unenforceable, such invalidity shall not affect the remaining clauses, provisions or parts of this Will, which shall continue in full force and effect, and this Will shall be construed as if the invalid clause, provision or part had never been contained herein, so far as is consistent with my intentions as expressed in this Will. This Will shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the Indian Succession Act, 1925, the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, and other applicable laws of India.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF I, Rajesh Mehra, have hereunto set my hand to this my last Will and Testament, comprising [NUMBER OF PAGES] pages, on this [DATE] day of [MONTH], [YEAR], at [PLACE OF EXECUTION, e.g., Kolkata].

SIGNED by the said RAJESH MEHRA, the Testator, as his last Will and Testament, in our joint presence, and then signed by us, in the presence of the Testator and of each other, as attesting witnesses.

TESTATOR'S SIGNATURE: ______________________
Name: Rajesh Mehra
Address: [ADDRESS]

WITNESS 1
Signature: ______________________
Name: [WITNESS 1 FULL NAME]
Address: [WITNESS 1 ADDRESS]
Occupation: [WITNESS 1 OCCUPATION]

WITNESS 2
Signature: ______________________
Name: [WITNESS 2 FULL NAME]
Address: [WITNESS 2 ADDRESS]
Occupation: [WITNESS 2 OCCUPATION]

Note: Neither witness should be a beneficiary under this Will or the spouse of a beneficiary. Both witnesses must be present together at the time the Testator signs, and must then sign in the presence of the Testator and of each other.

assumptions.assumption: Rajesh Mehra's father's name, full residential address in Kolkata, and other identifying particulars have not been supplied and are shown as placeholders.
assumptions.why: The facts did not include these particulars; they are required for the Declaration and execution block.

assumptions.assumption: Full descriptions of the Kolkata flat and Siliguri plot (survey/plot/khatian numbers, registration particulars) have not been supplied.
assumptions.why: The facts gave only value and location in general terms; precise legal description is required for a Will to operate on immovable property without ambiguity.

assumptions.assumption: Bank names, account numbers, FDR numbers, mutual fund folio numbers and AMC names have not been supplied.
assumptions.why: Only aggregate approximate values were given in the facts; exact identification is needed for the Schedule of Assets.

assumptions.assumption: The number of equity shares, face value and CIN of Mehra Trading Private Limited have not been supplied.
assumptions.why: Only the percentage shareholding (30%) was given; exact share particulars are required for a clean bequest and transmission.

assumptions.assumption: Rajesh Mehra has no dependants other than his wife, son and daughter, and no prior marriage, adopted child, or other dependant.
assumptions.why: The facts did not exclude this expressly; it is assumed for the Family and Dependants section and flagged for confirmation.

assumptions.assumption: The asset values stated (Rs. 1.5 crore, Rs. 80 lakh, etc.) are treated as the testator's own asserted approximate values as of the date of the Will, not as verified valuations.
assumptions.why: The facts describe these as approximate; no valuation report was provided.

assumptions.assumption: The permitted lease term for the life tenant (Sunita) under the life interest restriction has been left as a placeholder rather than fixed at a specific period.
assumptions.why: No instruction was given on whether short-term leasing should be permitted to the life tenant; this is a policy choice for the client.

drafting_notes.issue: Probate requirement for this Will has not been asserted either way in the document, consistent with the instruction not to state a blanket rule. Under s. 213 read with s. 57 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, probate of a Hindu's Will is compulsory only where the Will is made within the local limits of the ordinary original civil jurisdiction of the Calcutta, Madras or Bombay High Courts, or relates to immovable property situated within those limits.
drafting_notes.recommendation: Since the testator resides in Kolkata and owns immovable property there, the Will likely falls within the ordinary original civil jurisdiction of the Calcutta High Court, making probate compulsory as to the Kolkata flat and possibly the whole estate. Confirm the precise jurisdictional position (i.e., whether the flat falls within the local limits of the Calcutta High Court's ordinary original civil jurisdiction) before advising the client on probate necessity, and advise that the Siliguri land situated outside those limits may not independently attract the requirement.

drafting_notes.issue: Transmission of the 30% shareholding in Mehra Trading Private Limited to Arjun and Riya is subject to the company's Articles of Association, which commonly contain pre-emption or transfer-restriction clauses even on transmission by will/succession.
drafting_notes.recommendation: Obtain and review the Articles of Association of Mehra Trading Private Limited before or shortly after execution of the Will, to confirm whether transmission to legal heirs is unrestricted or subject to Board/member approval, and advise the client accordingly. The bequest clause has been drafted to expressly flag this subject-to qualification.

drafting_notes.issue: The life interest and restraint on alienation clause leaves the permitted lease term (if any) for the life tenant as an open placeholder.
drafting_notes.recommendation: Ascertain from the client whether Sunita Mehra should have any power to grant short-term leases (e.g., not exceeding eleven months, consistent with registration exemption practice) or whether the restraint on alienation should be absolute with no leasing power at all, and finalise the clause accordingly.

drafting_notes.issue: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 fallback in the survivorship clause (paragraph 3) triggers only in the remote scenario that both children predecease the testator without surviving descendants; the exact class of heirs who would then inherit has not been enumerated.
drafting_notes.recommendation: This is intentionally left to operate by reference to the statute rather than naming specific heirs, since no facts were given about further relatives. If the client wishes to name specific fallback beneficiaries instead of relying on intestate succession rules, obtain those names.

drafting_notes.issue: No residence, occupation or other identifying details for the two attesting witnesses have been supplied, and no witnesses have yet been identified.
drafting_notes.recommendation: Ensure two independent, competent witnesses (neither a beneficiary nor a beneficiary's spouse) are identified and are present together with the testator at the time of signing, in compliance with s. 63 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, and that their particulars are filled into the execution block before signing.

drafting_notes.issue: The instruction requested a severability/general provisions clause; this has been added as an additional section beyond the mandatory skeleton, named GENERAL PROVISIONS AND SEVERABILITY, placed after the Executor section and before Attestation.
drafting_notes.recommendation: No action needed; this fulfils the client's express instruction for a severability clause while keeping the mandatory skeleton sections intact and in order.

drafting_notes.issue: Valuations of all assets are recorded as the testator's own asserted approximate figures, not as documented or independently verified valuations.
drafting_notes.recommendation: For probate and stamp/succession purposes, obtain updated valuation reports or documentary evidence (bank statements, mutual fund statements, jewellery valuation certificate, property valuation) closer to the time of the testator's death, since values will change and the Will itself does not depend on the stated figures being accurate.
